text.p: Australian Provincial Newspapers Ltd (APN) had a tough but pleasing year in calendar 1996 and is optimistic about 1997, chief executive Cameron O'Reilly said.
"All I can say is that 1996 was a tough year but we are pleased with the outcome and we are optimistic about 97," O'Reilly told reporters on Tuesday after launching APN's Internet service.
APN, which is 49 percent owned by Irish media group Independent Newspapers Plc, reported a net profit of A$26.39 million for the 1995 calendar year, up from A$21.33 million in 1994.
The Australian group is expected to report its 1996 year results in early March.
At 1.40 p.m. (0240 GMT), APN shares were three cents down at A$2.25 in light volume.
